summary.intent: Clean up old git branches/worktrees, then work through a multi-step plan for the caliper repo: baseline weekly benchmark run, four tracked trails, schema v4 (readonly/index signatures/ref kind), detection-by-shape, and on-demand tsc hardening, each as its own PR.
summary.outcome: Cleaned 142 merged branches (two worktrees with uncommitted files left). Baseline run recorded on trail #125, schema v4 PR #266 and detect-by-shape PR #267 opened and marked ready, and the tsc-hardening branch was linted, tested and had its signed commit created; push, trail #128 link and PR were still pending when the transcript ended.

repo: Schema bumps follow a template: ADR 0023 (schema v3) shows the file footprint, a changeset, TS reader bumps, trycmd updates, napi typings and serialization-formats docs.
Snapshot tests resolve node_modules relative to the checkout, so a fresh worktree must install node deps or snapshots pick up a different @types/react and show path noise/spurious diffs.
Repo lint recipes: clippy without --all-targets, oxfmt/oxlint, doc-check, and typos; typos flags scratch files and words like 'alikes'.
Commits are signed and verified (signature status 'G'); pushing a branch and linking it to a trail via entire causes a draft PR to be opened automatically, which is then filled in and marked ready.
`just bench` compares time/RSS against origin/main; results are judged within noise (~1.0x).
The union normalizer already drops `| undefined` from values, so tests expecting it must expect the plain type.
Real-tsc tests skip locally when tsc is absent; CI was changed to fail on missing tsc instead of skipping.
The sandbox blocks `ps`, so RSS-cap tests need to run outside the sandbox.
Chakra has no unreduced NonNullable without dependencies loaded; NonNullable reduces fine for local unions.

code.finding: Index signatures `[key: string]: T` became object fields named `key` and were wrongly read as props by props-base code; consumers of object fields must skip index-signature fields.
Wrapper detection (forwardRef/memo, memo(forwardRef(fn))) was name-based and was made import-source-aware via a ReactApi binding.

The tagged-factory `{Name}Props` heuristic was replaced by a shape rule that must skip props types already claimed by another component in the file (e.g. Chakra's private StyledGroup recipe) to avoid false positives.

workflow: For unexpected snapshot diffs, bisect by temporarily reverting one change (e.g. peeling readonly) and compare against a baseline patch run in the same environment.
Before and after comparisons of component sets on real corpora (Chakra, Mantine) caught a false positive that unit tests missed.
Delegating a read-only root-cause analysis to a separate agent in its own worktree lets implementation proceed in parallel.
Use one worktree and one PR per trail item; keep earlier worktrees when moving on.

friction: Earlier file listing was a stale checkout, wrongly suggesting the weekly workflow was missing.
The harness required literal script paths and simpler commands, forcing helper scripts in a job tmp dir and split commands.
Fresh worktrees lacked node_modules, causing misleading snapshot diffs until deps were installed.
Two agent worktrees had uncommitted files and could not be cleaned up.
Shell loops were disallowed or awkward, so a Python script was used for snapshot diffs.
A shadcn source path was off by one directory, requiring a rerun of the latency measurement.
Scratch files and the word 'alikes' tripped the typos check.
open_items: Finish tsc-hardening: push branch, link to trail #128, fill in and mark the PR ready.
The NonNullable detection item was parked pending evidence from a dependency-loaded run.
Two agent worktrees with uncommitted files remain for the user to review.
shadcn/antd recall gap root-cause findings were recorded on trail #125 and may need follow-up work.
